I felt that Abhishek Jain came across as someone who believed the others didn't know anything. Throughout the episode, he repeatedly made comments like *"Tamne kai khabar j nathi,"* which came across as quite dismissive. There seemed to be a lot of ego in the way he interacted with Deep, Chirayu, and Om.

As a viewer, I honestly felt uncomfortable and even a bit insulted while watching the entire episode. In comparison, I enjoyed Dhvanit's episode much more.

I appreciate that you all kept the conversation going despite the situation. Manan did a great job trying to balance things out and explain how seniors typically approach such situations. That helped, but the overall tone still felt quite disrespectful.

My sincere suggestion would be to avoid inviting guests who belittle the hosts or other participants. A healthy debate is great, but repeatedly putting people down doesn't make for an enjoyable viewing experience. I can only imagine how Deep and Chirayu must have felt during the recording.

Interestingly, the origin of 'cheers' is often linked to a tradition from centuries ago when kings and nobles invited one another to feasts. As a gesture of trust and courtesy, they would clink their glasses together, causing a small amount of each drink to spill into the other person's cup. This symbolized that neither drink had been poisoned, since both parties would be drinking the same mixture. Over time, this act became a sign of goodwill and friendship, which is why we still say 'cheers' before taking a drink today.

"Masoor Dal (Red Lentil) Dosa Recipe" Ingredients:- For the Dosa Batter: * Masoor Dal (Red Lentils): 1 cup * Green Chilies: 2–3 (adjust to taste) * Garlic Cloves: 3–4 * Salt: To taste (approx. 1/2 tsp for grinding + 1/2 tsp for adjusting later) * Water: 1/2 cup (plus more if needed for consistency) * Cooking Oil: For frying For the Toppings (Optional): * Onion: 1 medium, finely chopped * Tomato: 1 small, finely chopped * Fresh Coriander: A handful, chopped * Peri-Peri Masala or Podi Masala: To sprinkle For the Green Chutney: * Fresh Coriander Leaves: 1 bunch * Garlic Cloves: 2–3 * Green Chilies: 2 * Lemon Juice: 1 tsp * Roasted Chana Dal (Dalia) or Sev: 1–2 tbsp (for thickness) * Salt: To taste * Water: As needed Preparation Steps:- 1. Prepare the Batter: * Wash 1 cup of Masoor Dal thoroughly. * Soak the dal in room temperature water for exactly 15 minutes. Note: Do not soak for longer, as the dal will become too soft and the dosa won't be crispy. * Drain the water and wash the dal 4–5 times under running water. * Transfer the soaked dal to a grinding jar. Add green chilies, garlic, salt, and 1/2 cup water. * Grind into a completely smooth paste. If the batter is too thick, add a little more water until it reaches a pouring consistency. * Transfer to a bowl and add another 1/2 tsp of salt (adjust to taste). Mix well. 2. Prepare the Green Chutney: * In a blender, combine coriander leaves, garlic, green chilies, lemon juice, roasted chana dal (or sev), and salt. * Add a splash of water and blend until smooth. Set aside. 3. Cook the Dosa: * Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) over low-medium heat. * Lightly grease the tawa with a drop of oil and then wipe it off completely with a tissue paper. The surface should not be greasy. * Pour a ladleful of batter into the center of the tawa. Using the back of the spoon, spread it in a circular motion moving outwards. * For Veggie Dosa: Sprinkle chopped onions, tomatoes, coriander, and peri-peri masala on top while the batter is still slightly wet. * Drizzle a little oil around the edges and on top. * Cook on low-medium heat for about 3 minutes. Be patient; Masoor dal takes a bit longer to crisp up than rice dosa. * Flip (Optional): If you prefer it cooked on both sides like an Uttapam, flip and cook for 30 seconds. For a classic crispy dosa, cook on one side only until the base is golden brown and firm. 4. Serving: * Fold the dosa and serve hot with the prepared green chutney. 👍

Spicy Matar (Green Peas) Sandwich Recipe ​Ingredients:- ​For the Pea Filling: ​Fresh Green Peas: 1 cup (Fresh is preferred over frozen for better texture and flavor) ​Garlic: 3–4 cloves ​Green Chilies: 2 (adjust to spice preference) ​Oil: 1 teaspoon ​Salt: To taste ​For the Spicy Green Chutney: ​Fresh Coriander Leaves: 1 bunch ​Garlic: 2–3 cloves ​Green Chilies: 1–2 ​Lemon Juice: 1 tablespoon ​Roasted Chana Dal (Dalia): 1 tablespoon (or Sev Bhujia for thickness) ​Salt: To taste ​Water: A splash for grinding ​For Assembly: ​Bread Slices: 4 slices (White, Brown, or Sourdough) ​Cheese Slices: 2 slices ​Butter: For toasting ​Instructions:- ​1. Prepare the Pea Filling: ​Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a pan over medium flame. ​Add the garlic cloves and green chilies. ​Add the fresh green peas and a pinch of salt. ​Sauté for 3 to 4 minutes until the raw smell disappears. Do not overcook them; they should just be soft enough to grind. ​Remove from heat and let the mixture cool completely. ​Once cooled, transfer to a grinder and pulse a few times to get a coarse, grainy texture. Avoid making a smooth paste. ​2. Make the Green Chutney: ​In a blender, combine coriander leaves, garlic, green chilies, lemon juice, roasted chana dal, salt, and a little water. ​Blend into a thick, spicy chutney. ​3. Assemble the Sandwich: ​Take two slices of bread. Apply a generous, thick layer of the coarse pea mixture on both slices. ​Place a cheese slice on top of the pea filling on one of the bread slices. This helps balance the spiciness of the peas and chutney. ​On two separate bread slices (the "top" slices), spread a layer of the spicy green chutney. ​Close the sandwiches by placing the chutney-spread bread over the cheese and pea-covered bread. ​4. Toast to Perfection: ​Heat a tawa (griddle) over low flame to ensure the sandwich gets extra crispy. ​Spread some butter on the tawa and place the sandwiches on it. ​Press gently and cook until the bottom is golden brown. ​Apply butter on the top side of the bread before flipping. ​Flip carefully and toast the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes until both sides are golden brown and the cheese inside has melted. ​5. Serving: ​Cut the sandwiches diagonally. * ​Serve hot with tomato ketchup and a side of potato chips for a cafe-style experience. 👍
